# Reporting a security problem

**Do not open a public issue for a vulnerability.** An issue is readable by everybody the moment it is filed, including whoever would use it, and it stays readable in the timeline even after it is edited.

## How to report one

Use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting: [open a draft advisory](https://github.com/phranck/Playable/security/advisories/new). It is private between you and the maintainer, it needs no email address from either of us, and it turns into a published advisory if one is warranted.

If you cannot reach that page, open a public issue saying only that you have a security report and asking to be contacted. Say nothing about the problem itself.

## What helps

A report is easier to act on when it says what you did, what happened, and what you expected instead. Where it matters, add which part of Playable it concerns: the API, the website, the dashboard, or one of the desktop apps.

Please do not test against anything that is not yours. Playable stores what listeners follow and listen to, and a proof of concept run against real accounts is itself a problem.

## What to expect

You will get an acknowledgement. What follows depends on what the report turns out to be, and you will be told either way rather than left waiting.

There is no bounty programme and no payment. Playable is built by one person.

## Which versions this covers

Nothing has been released yet. The only version that exists is the default branch, so that is what a report is assessed against.
